no CO₂ emission | --- ### Quick Takeaways - **Hydrogen is the simplest, most abundant element** in the universe, existing as a diatomic gas (H₂) under normal conditions. - It has **unique physical properties**: very low density, extremely low boiling/melting points, and a high specific heat capacity. - Chemically, it is **highly reactive**: it burns readily, forms strong covalent bonds, and can act as both a proton donor (acid) and a hydride donor (base). - Its **isotopes** (deuterium and tritium) are crucial in nuclear science, medical imaging, and fundamental physics experiments. - In **astrophysics**, hydrogen fuels stars and is traced by the famous 21‑cm radio line. - In industry, hydrogen is a **clean energy carrier** (fuel cells, rockets) and a key reagent in many chemical processes.
